cards.stem: What is the relationship between wing area and lift when other conditions stay constant?
options: Doubling the area doubles the lift
Halving the area doubles the lift
Doubling the area halves the lift
Doubling the area has no effect
cards.quote: Doubling the area doubles the lift.

cards.stem: What does lift depend on as an aerodynamic force?
options: pressure variation of the air around the body
weight of the fuselage alone
temperature of the cockpit interior
color of the wing surface
cards.quote: Lift is an aerodynamic force and therefore depends on the pressure variation of the air around the body as it moves through the air.

cards.stem: How is planform area described for use in the lift equation?
options: area of the wing as viewed from above the wing
total surface area of top and bottom combined
area of the tail fin viewed from the side
area of the fuselage cross section
cards.quote: The planform area is the area of the wing as viewed from above the wing, looking along the “lift” direction.

cards.stem: Why do designers change wing area during takeoff and landing?
options: designers try to increase the wing area
designers try to decrease the wing area
designers try to keep the wing area constant
designers try to remove the wing area completely
cards.quote: Takeoff and landing are times of relatively low velocity, so to keep the lift high (to avoid the ground!) designers try to increase the wing area.
